cards.text: Jesus has spent the day teaching by the sea, and the crowd is still packed along the shore. Now evening comes. Jesus turns to His disciples, and He's got somewhere to be.

cards.question: When evening comes, where does Jesus tell His disciples they should go?

cards.text: So they send the crowd away and take Jesus with them, since He's already in the boat. Easiest boarding in history: no line, no ticket, He was just already sitting there.

cards.question: Out on the water that evening, the disciples' boat is the only boat with Jesus.
Not long after Jesus and His disciples set out across the sea, what comes up?

cards.text: Waves are breaking over the boat, and it's being swamped. Friend, that is not a boat anymore. That's a BATHTUB with oars.

cards.question: While the waves are swamping the boat, Jesus is asleep in the stern.

cards.text: Sleeping. On a cushion. Through THAT. Meanwhile back in the junk drawer, I jumped every time somebody rattled it looking for tape.

cards.question: The disciples wake Jesus up in the middle of the storm. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: Don't You care that we are perishing
Should we turn back to the shore now
Can You help us bail out this water

cards.text: And honestly? I respect it. I would've been right there shaking Him awake with my mustache, yelling "TEACHER! TEACHER! WE ARE GOING DOWN!"

cards.question: Awake now, Jesus gets up in the swamped boat. He rebukes the ___ and the sea.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks right to the storm. "Silence!" He commanded. "Be still!"

cards.question: Jesus commands the wind and the sea to be silent and still. What happens next?

answers.text: The wind dies down and it's perfectly calm
The waves stop but the wind keeps blowing
The storm slowly fades through the night

cards.text: Perfectly calm. From two commands. Friend, I tell my oven timer to hush every single day, and it has never ONCE listened.

cards.question: With the sea calm, Jesus turns to His disciples. His first question for them is: Why did you wake Me up?
Jesus asks His disciples why they're so afraid. Then He asks them: Do you still have no ___?
Once the sea is perfectly calm, the disciples' fear is gone too.

cards.text: Overwhelmed with fear, and the storm's already gone. I think they just figured out the storm was never the biggest thing in that boat.

cards.question: Overwhelmed with fear on the calm sea, what do the disciples ask one another?

answers.text: Who is this that even the wind and the sea obey Him
How are we ever going to get back to the shore
Where did such a terrible storm come from so fast

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "TEACHER! TEACHER! WE ARE GOING DOWN!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus spent the day teaching by the sea and the crowd is packed along the shore. That comes from Mark 4:1, which is outside the passage, but the card cites only Mark 4:35 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer "Don't You care that we are perishing" is the only emotional, accusing line, and "perishing" sounds more like the Bible. The wrong answers are calm, practical and modern ("bail out this water"). A baker could pick the right answer by its tone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card is only a reaction joke. It tells no new part of the passage and repeats the moment already covered on cards 8 and 9 (Mark 4:38).

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "disciples" can be argued as right. In Mark 4:40 Jesus corrects the disciples ("Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?"), and a baker could fairly say He rebukes them.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card repeats the answer to card 13 ("Perfectly calm. From two commands.") and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward, so it works as a recap card.

"The storm was never the biggest thing in that boat" points straight at Jesus. That rules out the wrong answers on card 19 about the shore and about where the storm came from, so the baker is steered to the answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
